description: The Federal Aviation Administration's Aeronautical Data Team collects, validates and publishes the aeronautical information that describes the physical layout, position, operating characteristics and status of every component of the US National Airspace System, following ICAO standards and the 28-day AIRAC cycle. The main national product is the 28-day National Airspace System Resources (NASR) subscription, downloadable free as TXT and CSV subscriber files for each cycle with an archive of past cycles; it covers airports and runways, navaids, fixes, airways, airspace, frequencies, location identifiers and related records, and changed format from the 3 September 2026 cycle. The Aeronautical Data Delivery Service (ADDS) publishes the same data as open GIS layers (73 items on 26 September 2026): airports, runways, airport mapping features such as aprons, taxiways and hotspots, ATS routes, airspace classes and boundaries, special use airspace, navaid and ILS systems, holding patterns, obstacles, VFR chart areas and pending versions of each, and the FAA also publishes UAS facility maps and national security UAS flight restrictions. Data are public, provided as is. Caveats: pending layers show future changes, several ADDS items are copies republished by others, and the files are not certified for navigation outside official products. The data give airport and airspace geometry for network flow, capacity planning and resilience studies of air traffic, airport capacity and airspace disruption models; OurAirports is a crowdsourced global counterpart.
